missing_methods.intent: Assert tell your experience text is truncated to characters
missing_methods.query: Assert tell your experience text is truncated to characters
missing_methods.detailed_requirements: This method should verify that the text entered in the 'tell your experience' feedback field is truncated to a maximum character limit. Steps: 1) Retrieve the current text from the feedback text field using get_entered_text() or similar method. 2) Get the character count of the retrieved text. 3) Compare the actual character count with the expected_max_length parameter. 4) Assert that the text length does not exceed the expected maximum. 5) Optionally verify the character count display matches the actual count. 6) Return True if assertion passes, raise AssertionError with descriptive message if it fails. The method should handle edge cases like empty text or text exactly at the limit.
missing_methods.rationale: While feedback.py has get_feedback_text_char_count() to retrieve the character count display and get_entered_text() to get the text, there is no explicit method to assert that the text is properly truncated to a specific character limit. This assertion logic belongs in feedback.py as it directly relates to feedback text input validation.
